intro: In the Common Core standards, this skill is marked 'not applicable' to literature because it deals with evaluating arguments, which belong to informational text. We can still build the underlying thinking with stories. Here you will read a passage, then decide which statements about it are supported by evidence in the text and which are just opinions a reader might hold.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Maya had practiced the violin for three years, but she still froze whenever she performed for an audience. At the spring concert, her hands shook so badly that she dropped her bow during the second measure. She bent down, picked it up, took a slow breath, and started again. This time she played the whole piece without stopping. Afterward her teacher said, 'You did the hardest thing a musician can do. You recovered.'

Claim A: Maya has been playing violin for three years. Claim B: Maya is the most talented student in her class. Which claim is supported by evidence in the text, and which is an unsupported opinion?

steps: Check each claim against the actual words of the passage.
Claim A: the text states 'Maya had practiced the violin for three years.' This is directly stated.
Claim B: the text never compares Maya to other students or mentions her ranking. It is an opinion a reader might guess but cannot prove from the text.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported by evidence. The text directly states she had practiced for three years. Claim B is an unsupported opinion, because the passage never compares Maya to other students or describes her as the most talented.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The old lighthouse had not been used in forty years. Its paint had peeled, and gulls nested in the broken windows. But every evening, Mr. Alvarez climbed the spiral stairs and polished the great glass lens until it shone. 'Ships do not need it anymore,' his granddaughter said. 'I know,' he answered. 'But I do.'

Claim A: Mr. Alvarez polishes the lens because it gives his life meaning. Claim B: The lighthouse has been out of use for forty years. Which is text-supported and which requires inference beyond what the text proves?

steps: Claim B: the text states 'The old lighthouse had not been used in forty years.' Directly stated.
Claim A: Mr. Alvarez says 'But I do,' suggesting he needs the routine, but the text never states it 'gives his life meaning.' That is an interpretation.
An interpretation can be reasonable yet still go beyond what the text directly proves.
solution.answer: Claim B is directly supported. The text states the lighthouse had not been used in forty years. Claim A is a reasonable interpretation but is not directly stated, so it goes beyond what the text proves; it is closer to opinion than fact.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Dev signed up for the cooking club even though none of his friends did. On the first day, he burned the rice and forgot the salt. By the fifth week, the teacher asked him to help the newer students. 'How did you get so good so fast?' one asked. Dev shrugged. 'I just kept showing up,' he said.

Claim A: Dev improved at cooking over five weeks. Claim B: Dev is naturally gifted at cooking. Which claim does the text support?

steps: Claim A: the text shows him burning rice in week one and helping others by week five. The improvement is shown through evidence.
Claim B: Dev says 'I just kept showing up,' which suggests effort, not natural gift. The text actually points away from Claim B.
A claim can be contradicted by the text, not just unsupported by it.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported. The text shows Dev struggling in week one and helping others by week five. Claim B is unsupported and even contradicted, because Dev attributes his progress to persistence ('I just kept showing up'), not natural talent.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The storm knocked out the power for three days. At first the children complained about the dark and the cold. But by the second night, the family was telling stories by candlelight, and Grandma taught everyone a card game she had played as a girl. When the lights finally came back on, eight-year-old Rosa said, 'Can we turn them off again?'

Claim A: The family found unexpected joy during the blackout. Claim B: The blackout lasted three days. Identify which is fact stated in the text and which is an interpretation.

steps: Claim B: the text states 'The storm knocked out the power for three days.' Directly stated fact.
Claim A: the storytelling, the card game, and Rosa's question suggest joy, but 'unexpected joy' is an interpretation built from those details.
Interpretations are supported when several details point to them, even if the exact words are not used.
solution.answer: Claim B is a directly stated fact: the power was out for three days. Claim A is an interpretation, but a well-supported one, because multiple details (storytelling, the card game, Rosa wanting the lights off) point to the family finding joy.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Jamal's older brother had warned him that the new school would be lonely. For the first week, Jamal ate lunch alone. Then he noticed another boy sketching at the next table and asked what he was drawing. By Friday they were sharing a table, and by the next month Jamal had a small group of friends who met every day.

Claim A: Jamal's brother is a dishonest person. Claim B: Jamal made friends within about a month. Which claim can the text support, and why is the other unsupported?

steps: Claim B: the text shows Jamal alone in week one and with a group 'by the next month.' Supported by the timeline in the text.
Claim A: the brother warned the school 'would be lonely,' and it was lonely at first. Calling the brother 'dishonest' is an opinion the text does not justify.
Being wrong about a prediction is not the same as being dishonest; the text gives no evidence of dishonesty.
solution.answer: Claim B is supported by the text's timeline, which shows Jamal alone at first and part of a group within a month. Claim A is unsupported, because the text never suggests the brother lied; he simply made a prediction that did not fully come true.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Tariq promised his little sister he would teach her to ride a bike before summer ended. Every evening after his job at the market, he ran alongside her as she wobbled down the street. On the last day of August, she pedaled half a block on her own, and Tariq cheered so loudly that the neighbors looked out their windows.

Claim A: Tariq kept his promise to his sister. Claim B: Tariq dislikes his job at the market. Which claim is supported by the text?
items.hint: Check whether each claim is actually stated or shown in the passage.

steps: Claim A: he promised to teach her before summer ended, and she rode on the last day of August. The text shows the promise kept.
Claim B: the text mentions his job but says nothing about how he feels about it.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported, because the text shows Tariq teaching his sister and her succeeding before summer ended. Claim B is unsupported, since the passage never says how Tariq feels about his job.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

The science fair judges walked slowly past each project. When they reached Lin's display about water filtration, they stopped and asked three questions. Lin answered each one calmly, pointing to her charts. She did not win first place, but the head judge wrote on her card, 'The clearest explanation of the day.'

Claim A: Lin understood her project well. Claim B: Lin was disappointed she did not win. Which claim does the text support, and which is an assumption?
items.hint: Look for evidence of understanding versus evidence of feelings.

steps: Claim A: she answered three questions calmly and earned praise for the clearest explanation. The text supports understanding.
Claim B: the text never describes Lin's feelings about not winning. Disappointment is assumed, not shown.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported, because Lin answered the judges' questions and was praised for the clearest explanation. Claim B is an assumption, since the text never states or shows that Lin felt disappointed.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Grandfather kept a garden behind the apartment building. The other tenants thought it was a waste of the small yard, but every August he filled baskets with tomatoes and peppers and left them by the mailboxes for anyone to take. By the end of the summer, even the people who had complained were carrying the vegetables home.

Claim A: Grandfather shared his vegetables with neighbors. Claim B: Grandfather grew the best vegetables in the city. Which is supported and which is opinion?
items.hint: One claim is shown by an action; the other is a comparison the text never makes.

steps: Claim A: he 'left them by the mailboxes for anyone to take.' Directly shown.
Claim B: the text never compares his vegetables to anyone else's in the city.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported, because the text shows Grandfather leaving vegetables for neighbors to take. Claim B is an unsupported opinion, since the passage never compares his garden to others in the city.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

Nadia had never spoken in front of the class without her voice trembling. When the teacher assigned oral reports, Nadia practiced in front of her mirror every night for two weeks. On the day of her report, her voice still shook at the start, but she finished every sentence and even answered a question at the end.

Claim A: Nadia prepared carefully for her report. Claim B: Nadia will become a famous speaker someday. Which claim can be supported with evidence from the text?
items.hint: Future predictions usually cannot be supported by a passage about the present.

steps: Claim A: she 'practiced in front of her mirror every night for two weeks.' Directly stated.
Claim B: the text describes one report, not her future. The prediction goes far beyond the evidence.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported, because the text states Nadia practiced every night for two weeks. Claim B is unsupported, since a prediction about her becoming famous goes far beyond anything the passage shows.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

When the animal shelter flooded, volunteers came from all over town to move the dogs and cats to dry ground. A boy named Oscar, who had wanted a pet for years, spent the whole day carrying crates. At the end, the shelter director offered him a kitten for free. Oscar looked at it for a long moment, then said, 'Give it to someone who hasn't had a hard week. I just came to help.'

Claim A: Oscar helped at the shelter during the flood. Claim B: Oscar did not really want a pet. Which claim is text-supported, and why is the other contradicted?
items.hint: Re-read what the text says about Oscar's long-held wish.

steps: Claim A: he 'spent the whole day carrying crates.' Directly shown.
Claim B: the text says Oscar 'had wanted a pet for years,' so claiming he did not want one is contradicted by the text.
solution.answer: Claim A is supported, because the text shows Oscar carrying crates all day. Claim B is contradicted, since the text states Oscar had wanted a pet for years; his refusal shows generosity, not a lack of desire.
